notes: Independent answers produced without reading data/questions/** or content-cards. Only reviews/blind/H.json was consulted. H-WQUANT-013 was flagged upstream as having a correctAnswers array bug fix; I answered independently and will cross-check in Phase B. Quantization scope distinctions (kernel-level vs end-to-end speedup) were tracked explicitly per question.

answers.rationale: A FP16/BF16 halves memory + doubles BW utilization vs FP32. C FP32 accumulator mitigates FP16/BF16 sum overflow/cancellation. D FP32->FP16 downcast introduces rounding per element. B false: FP16/BF16 TC has 2x+ throughput vs FP32 TC on Ampere+.
Classic swamping in FP16 reduction; once running sum exceeds ~2^k, values below ~2^(k-11) become invisible due to 10-bit mantissa. FP32 partial sums accumulated while small fix this.

A ~1% salient channels identified by activation magnitude. B per-channel scaling shrinks salient weights, activation scale absorbed by preceding op. C W4A16, no activation calibration. D false (AWQ != GPTQ Hessian-based). E false (dequant-in-register to FP16 works on any FP16 TC GPU).
B MinMax simplest but outlier-sensitive. C Percentile trims extremes. D KL/entropy calibrator used by TensorRT. A false — MinMax is often the LEAST accurate due to outliers.
Sign-extend each nibble to signed int, __int2half_rn to FP16, apply per-group FP16 scale => FP16 vector for FP16 TC matmul. HBM traffic ~4x reduction vs FP16, compute stays on FP16 TC.
FP32 = (1,8,23); FP16 = (1,5,10); BF16 = (1,8,7). BF16 keeps FP32's exponent (8-bit) but has narrower 7-bit mantissa.
BF16 uses 8-bit exponent (FP32-range), 7-bit mantissa. Fixes gradient underflow that FP16's 5-bit exponent could not handle.
TF32: 1 sign + 8 exponent + 10 mantissa = 19 bits. Storage remains FP32; only the TC multiplier truncates mantissa on input; accumulator FP32.
Dynamic quant computes activation scale from tensor stats at each forward pass; static quant freezes scales offline via calibration.
Forward is correct fake-quant (round + clamp + rescale). round's derivative is zero a.e.; STE approximates d(round(x))/dx ~ 1 on clamp interior => gradients pass through.

A E4M3 narrow range, higher precision => forward activations/weights. B E5M2 wider range, lower precision => gradients. C both 8 bits total. D false (scaling required for FP8). E false (Ampere has NO FP8 TC).

A H100 FP8 ~2x BF16 peak. C FP8 QMMA uses FP32 accumulator regardless of E4M3/E5M2 input. D per-tensor/per-block scaling required; TE DelayedScaling automates. B false (FP8 accumulator would be catastrophic).
At M=1 decode, kernel is bandwidth-bound: weight matrix K*N loading dominates regardless of activation dtype. INT8 TC peak advantage cannot be realized.
GPTQ: column-by-column weight quantization with Hessian-based (H ~ 2 X^T X) second-order error compensation to remaining unquantized columns.

A per-tensor: 1 scale, simplest, outlier-sensitive. B per-channel: one per row, epilogue applies. C per-group: subdivide in_channels, group=128 canonical for W4A16. D false (per-channel usually more accurate). E false (per-group is standard practice for W4A16).
NumPy/PyTorch broadcasting aligns from the LAST axis. scale.shape=(out,) with W.shape=(out,in) => tries to broadcast on `in` dim => per-input-channel scaling, incorrect. Fix: scale.unsqueeze(1).

Stem explicitly specifies symmetric convention [-127,127] and [-7,7] (excluding -128/-8 to keep range symmetric around zero, matches TensorRT/PyTorch symmetric quant). D uses full two's-complement [-128,127] which is asymmetric.

A INT4 KV kernel support less mature; often INT4 storage + FP16 dequant in attention. C INT4 halves memory vs INT8 = 4x vs FP16. D INT4 KV accuracy drop grows with context length due to softmax sensitivity. B false — INT4 is coarser, generally less accurate than INT8.

A INT8 TC on Turing+. B FP8 TC only Hopper/Ada. C W4A16 uses FP16/BF16 TC after dequant. D false (INT4 TC never a headline path; W4A16 speedup comes from FP16 TC + reduced HBM). E false (software emulation on CUDA cores rarely gives speedup vs FP16 TC path).
KV cache quant primary target: reduce per-request KV memory footprint (long context / large batch capacity); secondary: reduce attention memory BW when kernel reads quantized KVs.
Quantization error accumulates in softmax over long contexts (32K attended positions); at 4K negligible. Trade-off favorable if drop is acceptable and batch/context gain valuable.

A native quantized KV kernel gives both storage + BW savings. B eager dequant to FP16 in a separate kernel loses BW savings (FP16 buffer still read). D dequant-in-register saves storage + still saves BW (INT8 HBM read < FP16). C false (mixed FP16-weights/INT8-KV is common).

14 GB / 3.6 GB ~ 4x weight-load traffic reduction; batch-1 decode dominated by weight loading => decode speed improves by close to same factor minus dequant overhead. Kernel-level BW-bound speedup, not compute-bound.

A dynamic loss scaling shifts grad into FP16 range. B BF16 removes need for loss scaling (mostly). C forward matmul: FP16 inputs, FP32 accum, FP16 output. D FP32 master weights preserve small-gradient updates.
Outliers dominate per-tensor MinMax scale; 99% of values compressed into ~5 levels out of 254. Per-channel activation quant or SmoothQuant fix by shifting outlier magnitude to weights.
FP16 max ~6.5e4; 4096-term reduction can overflow. FP32 range ~3.4e38 easily holds intermediate. FP16 output on downcast.
PTQ: no retraining, calibration set determines scales. QAT: fake-quant ops in training graph => model learns quantization-robust weights, typically higher accuracy at low bits.
STE approximates d(round)/dx ~ identity on clamp interior. Works well for INT8; noisier at INT2/INT3, motivating PACT/LSQ that learn step size.
RNE: IEEE-754 default, ties to even, deterministic. Stochastic rounding: probabilistic in proportion to distance; unbiased estimator, useful for low-precision gradient accumulation.
Saturation clamps to boundary (preserves ordinality, correct for DNN). Wrap-around modular arithmetic flips signs catastrophically for signal-carrying activations.
Standard affine quantizer: q = round(x/s) + z; dequantize x_hat = (q - z) * s.
SmoothQuant: per-channel diagonal scaling s. Y = X W = (X diag(1/s)) (diag(s) W); activation outlier magnitude migrated to weights. Since weights easy to per-channel-quantize, W8A8 becomes tractable.
Symmetric z=0 simplifies GEMM (no cross-term); good for weights (roughly zero-centered). Asymmetric captures skewed distributions (e.g., post-ReLU) at cost of bias term.
Smaller group => more scales tracking narrower distributions => better accuracy but higher metadata BW. group=128 canonical default (~3% metadata overhead).

C W4A16 targets BW-bound decode; INT4 halves HBM traffic vs INT8, dequant-in-register keeps compute on FP16 TC. D W8A8 targets compute-bound, INT8 TC path. A false — W4A16 does NOT need INT4 TC; dequant to FP16 works. B false — W8A16 keeps activations in FP16, does NOT quantize activations (no calibration), and targets BW-bound not compute-bound.
